about: Stop Giving Me Your Toughest Battles is a two-character drawing. On the left, a withered, wrinkled Wojak with sunken eyes rests his cheek on his hand and pleads, "Stop giving me your toughest battles." On the right, Jesus is drawn in the square-jawed, side-profile Chad style, with long hair, a beard, a crown of thorns and a golden halo, calmly looking back at him. The blank space under Jesus is for his answer, which is always yet another ridiculous ordeal. It flips the old consolation line about strong soldiers getting the hardest fights into a joke about a life full of small, oddly specific trials.
origin: It parodies the old consolation line that God hands the hardest battles to the strongest soldiers, a sincere motivational phrase that has long been repeated ironically online. The Wojak-and-Jesus drawing turned that irony into a reply format.
usage:
There is one text box, under Jesus. Write the next battle he hands over, as if replying to the exhausted Wojak. The pleading line is already printed in the image, so the caption is only the punchline.

The best battles are petty, specific and painfully relatable: hardware that breaks at the worst moment, a teammate who never reads chat, a sock that keeps slipping off inside the shoe. Phrase it as a noun or a short scenario, not a full sentence, so it feels like an item being calmly handed over.
ideas: a printer that only works when IT is watching
a group project partner who replies once a week
a teammate who picks the same hero as you
a phone charger that only works at one angle
wifi that drops during the final boss
a sock that slides off inside your shoe
